title: Future Network Weimar Triangle: Science for Europe - Doctoral candidates (to Germany)
summary: Funding for doctoral candidates from France and Poland for research stays in Germany lasting three to twelve months, focusing on future-oriented topics and active participation in working groups.

subject_areas.notes: PhD students from all disciplines who are working on specific future-oriented topics.

institutions.notes: Universities or non-university research institutions in Germany.

nationality.notes: Targeted at applicants from France and Poland.

residence.notes: Applicants should not have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline. Individual doctorate in France or Poland.

mandatory.text: Applicants should not have graduated any longer than six years before the application deadline
Start of the doctorate should not be longer than 3 years ago
Not resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline
Active participation in one of the working groups throughout the scholarship period

funding.description: Monthly scholarship instalment of 1,400 Euros. Monthly lump sum for research expenses of 102 Euros. Additional benefits available under certain circumstances.

application_rounds.notes: The DAAD portal closes at 24.00 hrs. (CET or CEST) on the last application day. Source specifies Central European seasonal time. Unnormalised source clock time: 24.00.

required_documents.text: Full curriculum vitae in tabular form (max. 3 pages)
Letter of motivation for the chosen working group on the future-oriented topic (approx. 1 page)
Detailed description of the PhD project (5-8 pages)
University degree certificate and transcripts of records of your last academic degree
Declaration from the scientific supervisor in Germany on safety-relevant and ethical aspects
Confirmation from the academic host or the host institution in Germany
Proof of admission as a doctoral candidate at the home university
Summary of your final thesis (Master or equivalent) (approx. 1 page)
Proof of language proficiency (only if planning fieldwork/interviews in a language other than working language)
One recent letter of recommendation from a university teacher with DAAD cover sheet

steps.text: Request recommendation form and have it completed by a university teacher
Prepare application documents and translations if necessary
Fill out the application form and upload application documents in PDF format to the DAAD portal
